samples.summary: The case-insensitive `data:` fix in `imageInline` has no test
samples.evidence: The diff changes `image.src.startsWith('data:')` to `/^data:/i.test(image.src)` and the comment states this is "the one thing this branch exists to prevent" (a data URL emitted inline with `inlineImages` off). No test anywhere passes an uppercase/mixed-case scheme: I grepped `packages/docs/test` and `packages/cli/test` for `DATA:`/`Data:` and found no matches; `markdown.test.ts` only uses lowercase `data:image/png;base64,...` (lines 343, 361, 669). Because `SAFE_IMAGE_DATA_URI` is itself `/i`, reverting the fix would let `DATA:image/png;base64,…` be emitted inline with `inlineImages: false` and every existing test would still pass.

The new helper deliberately distinguishes page dimensions (0 rejected) from margins (0 accepted: "a margin of 0 is a legitimate edge-to-edge layout"). `packages/docs/test/import/docx-parser.test.ts` (lines 184-213) tests non-numeric, negative, zero and empty *page sizes* and non-numeric/negative *margins*, but never `<w:pgMar w:top="0" …>`. If `allowZero` were dropped or inverted, an imported edge-to-edge document would silently gain 96 px margins and no test would notice.

samples.summary: "a page-setup change is one undo step" cannot distinguish one undo step from two
samples.evidence: The test writes a setup then calls `editor.undo()` once and asserts `getPageSetup()` equals `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`. Since the document has no earlier page-setup edit, a `writePageSetup` that took two snapshots would also restore the default on the first undo — the assertion holds either way. The format-painter suite in the same PR (`editor-format-painter.test.ts`, "a paste is one undo step — no more, no fewer") explicitly establishes a distinguishable prior edit for exactly this reason; this test does not.

samples.summary: `fitMargins`' proportional scaling is asserted only as "> 0", so any clamp strategy passes
samples.evidence: `fitMargins` documents that it shrinks a margin pair *proportionally* "so a document whose margins are merely too large for its page keeps the ratio its author chose". The tests that exercise it (`types.test.ts` "leaves a positive content box when margins would close it" with a symmetric 5000/5000 pair, `docx-parser.test.ts` "leaves a positive content box when the margins swallow the page", also symmetric) only assert the content box is > 0. Resetting to defaults, zeroing both margins, or scaling equally would all pass; no test uses an asymmetric pair (e.g. 400/800) and checks the ratio survives.

samples.summary: `pasteFormat` firing `notifyStyleApplied()` is untested, unlike every sibling mutator
samples.evidence: The new API wrapper calls `notifyStyleApplied()` when a paste applied, with the comment "Same follow-up the toolbar's other style writes get". `packages/docs/test/view/editor-on-cursor-move.test.ts` has dedicated cases for `applyStyle`, `applyBlockStyle`/`clearFormatting`, `setBlockType`, `toggleList`, `indent`/`outdent` and the heading shortcut, but none for `pasteFormat`; `editor-format-painter.test.ts` never registers an `onCursorMove` listener. Losing the notification would leave toolbar pickers showing stale formatting after a paint, undetected.

samples.summary: Only CR/LF of the new `LINE_SEPARATORS` class are tested; NEL and U+2028/U+2029 are not
searchedFor: read the escaping describe block in markdown.test.ts

samples.summary: No test that a geometry the dialog accepts is one `setPageSetup` will not throw on
samples.evidence: The dialog rejects `left+right >= pageWidth` while `assertUsablePageSetup` throws on `left+right > width - MIN_CONTENT_PX`, and `handleSubmit` calls `editor.setPageSetup(...)` with no try/catch, so any geometry in the band between the two rules escapes as an uncaught RangeError from a React submit handler. `docs-page-setup-dialog.test.tsx` uses a `vi.fn()` `setPageSetup` that never throws, so no test exercises the two rules against each other (the docs-package test 'refuses a setup the resolver would silently rescale' covers the assert, but not the dialog's agreement with it).

samples.summary: The ruler margin-drag path, re-routed through the new asserting `writePageSetup`, has no test
samples.evidence: `ruler.onMarginChange` now calls `writePageSetup`, which runs `assertUsablePageSetup` and can throw inside a drag callback. Grepping for `onMarginChange` finds only `src/view/ruler/index.ts` and `src/view/editor.ts` — no test file — so nothing covers the refactored path. The ruler's own `minContent = 20` (ruler/index.ts:408) makes the throw unlikely in practice, which is why I grade this low.

samples.summary: Test named "writes the same targets to a file as it prints to stdout" never compares against stdout
samples.evidence: The case asserts only on `cap.files['out.md']`; `cap.stdout` is never read, so the stated equivalence between the file and the stdout path is not exercised. The individual assertions are real, but the test does not prove its title.
